summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout planning for ClearStream Health. Discussed cutover strategy (canary -> ramp -> full), A/B options, monitoring and runbook needs, security checks (SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts), and next steps for a staging dry-run. Agreed to exchange runbook/dashboards and finalize cutover date after staging run.
topics: Cutover strategy: canary percentage, ramp schedule
Monitoring and alert thresholds (latency P95, error rate, token cost)
Security: SSO/SAML, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-05 | Time: 16:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (ClearStream CTO), Sarah Kim (Sr ML Eng), Javier Lopez (DevOps)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check-in, how's the team doing?
[00:08] Daniel Ruiz: Good, Alex. Busy week. We ran the latest end-to-end with the staging replay, saw some latency blips but nothing blocking.
[00:16] Priya Patel: Cool — can you remind me which workload you were replaying, Daniel? Was it the longest-seq logs?
[00:23] Daniel Ruiz: Yeah, the patient-summary generator, the long ones, around 1.2k tokens usually. We saw P95 jump to ~420ms on single-node hosted config.
[00:33] Priya Patel: Okay that aligns with what we saw in the perf tests — long sequences push up memory and kernel switching. We'll go through cutover plan today.
[00:42] Sarah Kim: Quick note — quality looked consistent with the eval set, minor hallucination uptick on a specific prompt about medication dosages, we logged examples.
[00:50] Alex Chen: Thanks Sarah, please include those examples in the ticket. Alright agenda: cutover approach (canary vs A/B), monitoring/alerts, runbook, security checks, next steps.
[01:05] Javier Lopez: We also need to confirm SSO - we have strict SAML flows and corporate proxy, so dev ops needs to validate.
[01:12] Priya Patel: We can do SAML test accounts and a smoke auth flow in staging; Redwood supports SSO and audit logs — I can send the integration checklist.
[01:20] Daniel Ruiz: Great. On canary, we're thinking start small — 5% traffic for two hours, then 20% for four hours, then ramp to 50% overnight if metrics are green. Thoughts?
[01:31] Alex Chen: That's reasonable. We usually recommend 5-10% for an initial canary with a clear rollback window. Also define objective metrics for rollback.
[01:38] Priya Patel: Agree. Suggested auto-alert thresholds: P95 latency > 800ms, error rate > 1.5% 5m rolling, token-cost deviation > 20% vs baseline, and quality regressions flagged by your eval harness.
[01:52] Sarah Kim: For quality regressions, we can run prompt-set diffing and an automated diff on rouge/bleu-ish metrics and a set of hand-labeled prompts. If the delta exceeds X, we pause.
[02:02] Alex Chen: Perfect. We'll include those in the runbook. Who's responsible for the eval runner on your side?
[02:07] Sarah Kim: I'll own the eval runner and share results.
[02:10] Priya Patel: For the runbook, typical sections: pre-cutover checklist, canary steps, smoke tests (auth, latency, response correctness, downstream write checks), escalation path, rollback commands, and post-cutover validation.
[02:24] Javier Lopez: On rollback commands — for Dedicated customers we have ability to fail back to previous model variant or region; for hosted we can switch traffic back to prior model instance. Need exact steps.
[02:34] Priya Patel: I'll include step-by-step commands and the API curl examples. Also will specify how to pin to older model variant and how to trigger fallback to a cheaper locality.
[02:45] Daniel Ruiz: One more thing — can we run an A/B to compare model A (current) vs model B (quantized + tweaks) for response quality? Might help convince clinicians faster.
[02:56] Alex Chen: You can do A/B but keep in mind it complicates rollback and analysis. If you do A/B, tie it to user-facing KPI and keep groups small. Alternatively run parallel canaries and measure quality delta offline.
[03:09] Priya Patel: Operationally A/B requires tagging traffic and storing side-by-side logs. We can provision separate routes in the Redwood Console and dashboards for both variants.
[03:20] Sarah Kim: We prefer a canary-first approach and then an A/B for UX metrics. For clinicians we care about precision and hallucination rates more than raw latency.
[03:31] Alex Chen: Makes sense. On monitoring — we'll share sample Grafana dashboard links: latency P50/P95/P99, token cost per request, error traces, top failing prompts, and audit log stream for data access.
[03:44] Priya Patel: Also add KV cache hit-rate and batch-size distribution; those explain cost and latency variance.
[03:50] Javier Lopez: FYI our security team will want SOC2 docs and KMS/HSM details for key rotation.
[03:56] Priya Patel: Redwood has SOC2 and we can share the compliance pack. For keys we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations — I'll attach the architecture note.
[04:07] Daniel Ruiz: Great. Back to cutover timing — we're targeting mid-November, want to avoid month-end reporting. Tentative date 2026-11-20.
[04:15] Alex Chen: Sounds good. Recommend staging dry-run a week prior so we can rehearse rollback.
[04:20] Sarah Kim: We'll need replayed traffic in staging; Javier is on that.
[04:24] Javier Lopez: Yes, I'm fabricating a traffic replay from last month's logs and will feed to staging. Might need Redwood support to map headers for auth emulation.
[04:33] Priya Patel: We can provide a mapping script and a short token replacer to emulate SSO header flows. I'll share that.
[04:40] Alex Chen: Okay, quick run-through of the runbook smoke tests: 1) auth success 2) latency baseline within 20% 3) no increase in error rates 4) top-10 prompts should return within acceptable similarity threshold 5) downstream write ops succeed.
[04:55] Sarah Kim: For downstream writes, we need a sandbox write endpoint. Javier can set that up.
[05:00] Javier Lopez: Yup.
[05:03] Daniel Ruiz: On capacity — what happens if we need more throughput during the ramp? Can we burst into dedicated pool?
[05:10] Priya Patel: If you have Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity we can autoscale within the pool and add burst capacity; otherwise for hosted we can route to other regions or smaller model variants. We'll outline the cost implications.
[05:21] Alex Chen: Priya will send cost scenarios for 10/50/100% traffic. That'll help procurement sign-off.
[05:27] Daniel Ruiz: Perfect. Any open risks?
[05:30] Sarah Kim: The main risk is unseen quality regression on long-sequence prompts and SSO edge cases.
[05:35] Priya Patel: We'll include a checklist item for long-seq stress tests and a set of guard prompts that Sarah will feed us.
[05:43] Alex Chen: Escalation path: Level 1 - customer ops + Redwood support, Level 2 - Priya SE, Level 3 - Redwood on-call eng + CTO contact. Define SLAs for response times in runbook.
[05:56] Daniel Ruiz: Sounds good. Also please include contact numbers/emails for on-call.
[06:00] Priya Patel: We'll include a small page with paging steps and runbook snippets in the doc we send.
[06:07] Alex Chen: Final item — procurement. Daniel, where are you on PO and contract?
[06:12] Daniel Ruiz: Procurement needs the cost scenarios and a short appendix about data residency and encryption. We should have a finalized SOW by the 16th.
[06:21] Alex Chen: We'll push the procurement appendix along with SOC2/compliance pack.
[06:25] Priya Patel: Anything else on monitoring thresholds?
[06:28] Sarah Kim: Add an alert for sudden increase in hallucination flags from the eval runner. That's become our early warning.
[06:34] Priya Patel: Good call — we'll hook that into the alerting.
[06:37] Alex Chen: Alright before we wrap — recap of next steps: Alex send runbook template and dashboard links; Priya send capacity/cost + mapping script; Sarah run evals and share flagged prompts; Javier prep staging replay and SSO test accounts; Daniel confirm procurement cadence.
[06:58] Daniel Ruiz: All good. Thanks team.
[07:01] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and Slack, and I'll attach the runbook doc. Bye.
[45:00] Meeting ended
notes: Staging dry-run emphasized as critical step before cutover
Runbook will include explicit rollback criteria and escalation contacts
Quality guard prompts and eval runner integration are high priority
